newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hanoi foreign minister seeks closer Canberra ties.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi foreign minister seeks closer Canberra ties.

text.p: Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam arrived in Australia on Sunday for a three-day visit aimed at strengthening ties and boosting trade and investment, Australian officials said.

Cam held a series of private meetings in the southern city of Melbourne. He is due to fly to Canberra on Monday, where he will meet Prime Minister John Howard, Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer and other senior government members.
He will also meet Foreign Minister Alexander Downer for talks on bilateral and regional issues, the officials said.
Cam will meet leading business people and Vietnamese community leaders before leaving Australia on Tuesday.
He is the most senior Vietnamese official to visit Australia since a troubled tour by Communist Party chief Do Muoi in mid-1995. That visit was marked by a series of anti-Vietnamese protests.
Australia is home to a large expatriate Vietnamese community, many of whom fled south Vietnam after the Communist norths 1975 Vietnam war victory.
Canberra was one of the first Western countries to recognise Communist Vietnam and the two countries have a history of good relations despite their wartime enmity.
Both are keen to further boost trade, worth a total of A$527 million (US$405 million) in the year to June 30, 1996.

Bilateral relations have improved after coming under pressure early in the life of Australias year-old conservative government over Australian aid funding for a bridge across the lower Mekong River and plans to commemorate a Vietnam War battle.
